Well, Fuck. Cities + Erosion Laboratory 2.11: Toxic Sky & Rewilding

Collapses descend from high to low. Toxic skylight travels down open shafts and withers exposed growth. Radiation declines on a seed-dependent half-life; eventually the caverns can rewild with flowers. Fresh rubble remains charcoal-black for a long time.

Original illustrated cavern remains unchanged beneath a transparent simulation overlay. Click purple or black rock layers to open a crack, then advance the simulation. Black layers up to fourteen cells thick can now crack independently; green surfaces ride along with any detached rock. Fallen rock becomes dark, settles into rock by a randomly varied 0–2 cells, and remains bare for a long period before gradual, scattered moss growth. Openings left by detached material are transparent.

Speech communities

Buildings in the same settlement cluster share a language. Remote foundations inherit a parent language and then diverge. Phrase variants begin around turn 20; regular sound changes operate on IPA.

Experimental mechanics: only moved debris is drawn over the foreground illustration; detached source cells now cut openings through the original map. Ordinary rock collapse reveals a second, collapsible purple layer. When that layer or an original stalactite falls, the warm open chasm shows through. Debris stays nearly black for many turns, then can slowly develop a green surface layer when rock shelter and elevation permit. Large-scale stress, true fluid pressure and realistic fragment mechanics are not yet simulated. This is a geometry and dependency test.
